name: gauge

frames.best_why: All three rings show well-filled coloured arcs with distinct values and no cursor overlap.

tagline: Three circular dials fill with colour and show live numeric values.
summary: A set of radial gauges, each a full ring with a grey track and a coloured arc that fills to show its value. Large numbers sit in the middle with a small label below, and the values animate.
appearance: Three donut-shaped rings on a dark background, one blue, one violet and one green. Each has a dark grey track and a coloured arc starting at the top, a big white number centred inside and a small grey label underneath.
behaviour: Each coloured arc grows clockwise from the top to match its number, easing over about a second when the value changes. The demo re-rolls the values every 1.4 seconds.
demo_content: CPU, Memory and Disk I/O gauges with changing values like 72, 73 and 50.
use_when: A dashboard needs to show a few metrics as compact circular gauges with live values.
avoid_when: You need precise comparison between many values; circles are harder to read than bars.
customise: Set value, min, max, size, thickness and start/end angles, plus a getValueText formatter. Colours come from classes on the range and track.
weight_why: Three small SVG rings using a CSS stroke transition; no canvas or internal loop.

a11y.note: Each gauge exposes role meter with aria values and a label; the arc animation ignores reduced-motion.

issues: Values re-roll on a timer in the demo, so the circles never settle.
polish_why: Crisp rings and clear numbers; unprompted re-rolling values can distract.
